sampling_model.design: Complete randomization assigns exactly \(n_a\) of the \(N\) fixed units to each arm \(a\in\mathbb A\); the design is known and assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.units: The potential-outcome schedule \(x\in[0,1]^{3\times N}\) is fixed. The deterministic rounding theorem conditions on the full armwise empirical marginals \(F\); the statistical layer observes only one potential outcome per assigned unit.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed outcome is \(x_{Z_i i}\), and the estimator is the fixed contrast of arm means \(\widehat\theta_N=\sum_ac_an_a^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_i=a}x_{ai}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every arm size is positive and \(n_1+n_2+n_3=N\); endpoint consistency assumes \(n_a/N\to p_a\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each \(F_a\) is estimated by the simple-random-sample empirical law \(\widehat F_a\), then lifted to the equal-weight \(N\)-point law \(G_a\). Sampling error is controlled in \(W_1\) by exact hypergeometric variance, separately from deterministic rounding loss.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper obtains the exact partial identified set by optimizing over all marginal-compatible couplings and proves plug-in convergence for quadratic costs.
Lemma 1 gives sharp two-arm covariance bounds attained by comonotone and countermonotone quantile couplings.
The paper exhibits failure of the discrete quadratic Monge ansatz and asks for rigorous quantification of its error.
Theorem 3 proves strong NP-completeness of complete mixability, while the approximation result controls a bottleneck row sum.
The paper computes variance-maximizing causal completions by integer programming for broad assignment mechanisms and estimator classes.
Theorem 2.2 classifies the extreme points of the symmetric three-marginal, three-state Kantorovich polytope and includes non-Monge vertices.
Algorithm 3 rounds an approximately feasible tensor to the fractional transportation polytope, not to a Monge schedule.

body.tldr: Fractional multi-marginal transport can produce a sharper-looking three-arm variance bound than any \(N\)-unit potential-outcome table can realize.  For the bounded scalar contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), the worst same-empirical-marginal discrepancy is exactly of order \(N^{-1}\): arm-specific optimal-support slope grids, basic-table freezing, and hierarchical repair give a deterministic bit-polynomial schedule with loss less than \(402/N\), while an explicit four-row obstruction padded by isolated dummy rows loses exactly \(1/(46080N)\) for every \(N\ge4\).  Under complete randomization this finite-population operational correction becomes a computable \(O(N^{-2})\) band around the sharp upper variance endpoint, without contradicting Gao--Ge--Qian's superpopulation identified-set theorem.  Armwise empirical quantile lifts consistently estimate both variance endpoints while retaining the larger sampling-without-replacement error as a separate term.

project_justification.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) identify superpopulation causal variance bounds over fractional multi-marginal couplings, whereas a fixed population of \(N\) units requires one common \(N\)-row schedule; the distinction is operational and is not a contradiction of their theorem.  Emami and Pass (2025) demonstrate discrete non-Monge optimality and request quantitative error bounds in a different quadratic orientation.  Haus (2015) treats exact mixability and bottleneck approximation, and Brennan et al. (2025) rely on integer programming without an analytic realization width.
project_justification.niche: The unfilled object is the worst additive loss between a fractional optimum and an \(N\)-row optimum for the same three scalar \([0,1]\) empirical marginals and the fixed contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), together with an exact-rational construction polynomial in the input bit length.  The lower obstruction embeds into broader quadratic multi-marginal transport classes with \(K\ge3\) and \(d\ge1\), but the upper theorem is deliberately confined to this \(K=3,d=1\) class.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact arm-specific ordered dual-slope ranges, a multiscale exact-marginal repair algorithm with loss less than \(402/N\), an all-\(N\ge4\) rational lower family, and design-based endpoint certificates with explicit sampling-without-replacement plug-in error.

body.related_work: Emami and Pass (2025, Introduction, Example 1, and Discussion) move from the empirical Kantorovich relaxation to Monge implementability, prove a minimal non-Monge quadratic example, and identify quantitative approximation error as future work; their barycenter cost has the opposite squared-sum orientation from the signed scalar contrast here.  Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2 and Section 3) analyzes non-Monge extreme points in a symmetric finite transport polytope but gives no all-denominator additive rate.  Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) identify a superpopulation causal bound with fractional multi-marginal transport and prove plug-in rates; Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}variance\mbox{-}certificate}\) instead quantifies the operational error incurred when the same empirical marginals must be realized by one \(N\)-row fixed-population schedule, so the results are complementary rather than contradictory.  Haus (2015, Theorem 3 and the approximation section) proves hardness of exact matrix mixability and a bottleneck approximation result, objectives that do not subsume additive average squared-contrast rounding.  Altschuler and Boix-Adser\`a (2023, Algorithm 3) restore exact marginals after approximate tensor optimization but remain inside the fractional transportation polytope.  Puccetti and Wang (2015, Theorem 1.1 and Section 5) give the rearrangement representation and document unresolved higher-dimensional negative-dependence geometry; their discretization comparison changes the marginals rather than imposing same-\(N\) row realizability.  Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Lemma 1 and equations (7)--(11)) give sharp two-arm variance endpoints, recovered exactly by \(\mathrm{prop{:}two\mbox{-}arm\mbox{-}reduction}\).  Brennan et al. (2025, Sections 2--3) compute finite completions for general designs by integer programming and motivate an analytic certificate in the present restricted geometry.  Li and Ding (2017, Theorems 3--4) supply the fixed-potential-outcome complete-randomization framework, while Hammer et al. (1996) provide a concrete multi-arm trial consumer.  Adding zero coordinates and zero-coefficient arms embeds the lower obstruction into the broader \(K\ge3,d\ge1\) quadratic transport setting, but the \(O(N^{-1})\) achievability proof uses the note's exact \(K=3,d=1,[0,1]\) fixed-contrast geometry and does not transfer to arbitrary \(K,d\), or quadratic form \(A\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The improved universal constant \(402\) remains deliberately loose: \(402/N\) becomes strictly smaller than the trivial cost-gap bound \(1/4\) only at \(N=1609\), so the useful numerical report at ordinary trial sizes is the actual primal--dual width \([C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)]/(N-1)\).  The exact large-\(N\) constant remains open within \([1/46080,402]\), as does the extremal geometry.  The plug-in uncertainty band uses a first-moment Markov argument rather than a nonsmooth transport limit law, so sampling error dominates deterministic rounding error under proportional allocation.  Finally, only the lower obstruction automatically embeds into broader \(K\ge3,d\ge1\) quadratic transport classes; the achievability proof is specific to three scalar arms on \([0,1]\) and the fixed contrast.
body.honest_scope: The note proves the sharp \(N^{-1}\) order, the explicit constants \(1/46080\) and \(402\), the all-\(N\ge4\) lower family, the rational bit-polynomial algorithm, the finite-population variance translation, and the plug-in endpoint bounds.  It is an operational correction for realizing a fractional functional on one fixed \(N\)-unit science table, not a contradiction of a superpopulation identified-set result.  The lower obstruction extends to broader quadratic multi-marginal classes by adding zero coordinates and zero-coefficient arms, but the upper rate is proved only for \(K=3,d=1,[0,1]\) and \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\).  The theorem does not assert that one experiment observes all three full marginals, that every interior variance in the interval hull is attained, or that the unknown actual completion has variance at least \(U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)\).  The exact value of \(\Delta_3\) and the limit of \(N\Delta_N\) remain outside the proved result; the two-row realization loss is exactly zero.
